questions.question: What is React?

options.text: A JavaScript library for building UI

questions.explanation: React is a JavaScript library used to build user interfaces.

questions.question: What is a React component?

options.text: A function or class that returns UI

questions.explanation: Components are reusable building blocks of a React UI.

questions.question: Which command is used to create a React app?
questions.explanation: npx create-react-app is commonly used to bootstrap a React app.

questions.question: What is JSX?
questions.explanation: JSX allows writing HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript.

questions.question: Which hook is used to manage state?
questions.explanation: useState allows functional components to manage state.

questions.question: Which hook is used for side effects?
questions.explanation: useEffect handles side effects like data fetching.

questions.question: What is the virtual DOM?

options.text: A copy of the real DOM kept in memory

questions.explanation: Virtual DOM improves performance by minimizing real DOM updates.

questions.question: How do you pass data to a component?
questions.explanation: Props are used to pass data to components.

questions.question: Props are __________.
questions.explanation: Props are read-only and cannot be modified.

questions.question: What is state in React?
questions.explanation: State stores data that can change over time.

questions.question: Which hook is used to share data globally?
questions.explanation: useContext allows data sharing without prop drilling.

questions.question: What does useRef do?
questions.explanation: useRef is commonly used to access DOM elements.

questions.question: What is prop drilling?
questions.explanation: Prop drilling happens when props are passed through many layers.

questions.question: What is a controlled component?
questions.explanation: Controlled components use state to control form inputs.

questions.question: Which method renders JSX to the DOM?
questions.explanation: ReactDOM.render() renders React elements to the DOM.

questions.question: What is useReducer mainly used for?
questions.explanation: useReducer is useful for complex state logic.

questions.question: Which hook memoizes a function?
questions.explanation: useCallback memoizes functions.

questions.question: What is React.Fragment used for?

options.text: Grouping elements without extra DOM nodes

questions.explanation: Fragments group elements without adding extra nodes.

questions.question: Which key is required when rendering lists?
questions.explanation: Keys help React identify list items.

questions.question: Which library is commonly used for routing?
questions.explanation: React Router is used for navigation.

questions.question: What is lifting state up?
questions.explanation: Lifting state up helps share data between components.

questions.question: What is Redux mainly used for?
questions.explanation: Redux manages global application state.

questions.question: What does useMemo do?
questions.explanation: useMemo memoizes expensive computations.

questions.question: Which lifecycle method runs after component mounts (hooks)?
questions.explanation: useEffect runs after render.

questions.question: React is mainly used for?
questions.explanation: React focuses on building UI components.
